questions.q_en: In a row, Akash is 10th from the right end and Piyush is 8th from the left end. Jay is neighbour of both Akash and Piyush. How many persons are present in a row?
questions.solution_en:
In a row, Akash is 10th from the right end and Piyush is 8th from the left end.

Jay is neighbour of both Akash and Piyush.

Case 1: 7 persons - Piyush - Jay - Akash - 9 persons = 19 persons

Case 2: 5 persons - Akash - Jay - Piyush - 7 persons = 15 persons.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, two statements are given and two conclusions are given below these statements. Choose the option which shows the conclusions which logically follow from the given statements, disregarding the commonly known facts.

Statements:

All Java are Python

No Python is HTML

Conclusions:

I: Some Python is Java

II: No Java is HTML
options_en: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.solution_en:
Statements:

All Java are Python

No Python is HTML

Some Python is Java: All Java are Python. Thus, Some Python must be Java. So, conclusion I is true.

No Java is HTML: All Java are Python. No Python is HTML. Thus, No Java is HTML. So, conclusion II is true.

Hence, both conclusion I and conclusion II follow.

questions.q_en: Time shown in a clock is 8:29, what time will appear in the water?

Here, time is 8:29, so 1st formula is applicable.

Time in water = (18:30 - 8:29) = 10:01

questions.q_en:
One statement is given, and it is followed by two inferences numbered I and II. Read the statement and decide which of the inferences is/are true for the given statement.

Statements: Fuel prices in India are inflating day by day, and there is no upper limit in its price increase.

Inferences:

I. Central and State governments have not cut down their respective taxes on fuel.

II. Inflation in the international market is influencing the rising fuel prices.
options_en: Neither inference I nor II is true.
Both inferences I and II are true.
questions.solution_en:
The statement mentions that "Fuel prices in India are inflating day by day, and there is no upper limit in its price increase."

Rising fuel prices are not necessarily tied to the tax policies of the Central and State governments (as suggested in inference I) nor directly influenced by inflation in the international market (as suggested in inference II).

So, neither inference I nor II is true.

questions.q_en:
Each of the questions below consists of a question and two statements given below it. You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question:

How many students are there in the class?

Statement 1: In the class Shyam ranks 11th from the top and 23rd from the bottom.

Statement 2: Suresh ranks 10th above Raj, who is 18th from the top.
options_en: Statement 1 alone is sufficient to answer the question while statement 2 alone is not sufficient to answer the question
Statement 2 alone is sufficient to answer the question while statement 1 alone is not sufficient to answer the question
Either Statement 1 alone or statement 2 alone is sufficient to answer the question
Statements 1 and 2 are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution_en:
From 1:

Shyam ranks 11th from the top and 23rd from the bottom. Hence there are 11+23-1 = 33 students.

From 2:

Suresh ranks 10th above Raj, who is 18th from the top. This means Suresh is 8th. But it does not give the number of students.

Hence only 1 alone is sufficient.
